sources.entry: Posnic - Offline-first open source POS and billing software for retail shops and restaurants.

summary.one_liner: Posnic is a free, AGPL-3.0-licensed point-of-sale and billing app for retail shops and restaurants that runs its database and API on the shop computer or a server the owner controls.
summary.what_it_does: Posnic provides point-of-sale billing with keyboard and touch selling, barcode scanning, returns, part payments, held bills and quick sale. It covers stock management (items, variants, categories, purchases, supplier returns, inventory logs, low-stock alerts) and customer accounts with category pricing and outstanding balances. It produces GST invoices (IGST, CGST/SGST, HSN codes) and GST reports, plus restaurant features such as kitchen order tickets and table management. Reports cover sales, purchases, inventory, expenses, profit and staff activity, all exportable, and multiple branches are supported with per-branch stock and staff roles. The README says it can be installed as a Windows, macOS or Linux desktop app, or self-hosted on Ubuntu 24.04 via an install script that sets up Node.js, MongoDB and systemd.
use_cases: run a retail shop checkout offline
restaurant table and kitchen order management
GST invoicing and filing reports for India
self-hosted billing for a single shop on a local network
stock and inventory tracking across branches
free alternative to paid POS software
how_to_run: Desktop: download the packaged installer for Windows, macOS or Linux from the latest release and verify it against SHA256SUMS.txt
stack: MongoDB Community Server (7.0.14 fetched at build; 8 for self-hosting)
notable: Primary database and API run locally on the till or on a self-controlled server, with no Posnic account needed for the local edition
Posnic's own source is AGPL-3.0-only; bundled components such as MongoDB (SSPL-1.0) keep separate licences
Live demo available, with the shop restored hourly
Documented paths for thermal printers, scanners, cash drawers, scales and second displays, with a hardware matrix
Extensive operational checklists for backups, disaster recovery, cash reconciliation and incident response
caveats: Electronic payments, optional cloud services, downloads and integrations can still need a network
Multi-till sync and off-site backups are only in the paid Posnic Cloud service, not this repository
Self-hosting requires someone to maintain updates, backups and certificates; the README says a certificate and backup restore are needed before taking real payments
summary.license: AGPL-3.0-only (Posnic source); bundled third-party components carry their own licences, including SSPL-1.0 for MongoDB
